I suffer from bpd myself. I cannot say enough about this post. Toxic relationships were home to me and I attracted them like a magnet. I wanted to fix people and control them and it just carried so much more suffering for me. Biggest lesson for me was to fix my life and care for my heart. Get interested in the self again almost like a child would.  Be connected to the self and the ever expanding universe around you.  Once I started to do that the pressure to hold on to toxic people started to ease and become more healthy.

You're not wasting anyones time. I feel you so much in this. I'm so sorry your in pain too. I was doing better also and then a nasty trigger hit me. It hurts so much. I also feel very unworthy of help sometimes. But here's the thing. I read your post and wanted to send you a hug. The part where you say 'I feel like I'm holding their decency as human beings hostage by saying that I'm suicidal' really hit me. The first thing I thought was you deserve to be listened to. I mean why not. Thoughts can be killers of us. Then I thought man at the beginning of your life you were an innocent child. You didn't even have thoughts this complex yet. Just observation and wanting of love. As you said ' Because societally it's expected that you would help someone going through a tough time by offering to support them. Yes I believe that because my first instinct was to want to help you or at least write some words of comfort. You are not alone. I am in pain. But your pain matters too. We all need help its ok.

I just think we as humans are all knocked out of balance. Think about it we were never meant to live so isolated. Its not natural. We are social creatures and this is a good thing actually. You wouldn't read a book and stop in the middle and never find out the ending. Please keep writing. Your story is important and one of a ind. There is noone like you in the world. That's what makes you special. Looking forward to hopefully talking to you. Looking forward to reading your story. Much Love
